source.label: MicroCoach Wave 2 — Recommendation Pipeline, Evaluation Framework, and Evaluation Harness, §3a Misconception Rubric

description: The Misconception Rubric as data. Every misconception is scored 0–3 on each enabled metric; the highest total is the Recommended Focus. This file is the only place the bands, level definitions, cap and tiebreak live — scoreRubric.mjs reads it and does no arithmetic of its own.

metrics.label: Frequency
metrics.inputDescription: Share of students (0–1) who chose any wrong option linked to the misconception, counted from the response rows by computeMisconceptionReach.
metrics.scaleNote: Scored continuously rather than in the doc's four bands, which are kept above as docBands. The doc's top band begins above 50%, so 50% and over scores the maximum and below that the score is linear in share of class. Reason: the bands gave 29%, 39% and 43% the same score of 2, so several misconceptions tied on the total and the cap boundary was settled by a tiebreak rather than by reach.

metrics.label: Learning Progression Influence
metrics.description: Estimated influence of the underlying standard on future learning within the learning progression, operationalized for the Wave 2 pilot as the number of immediate buildsTowards relationships in the Learning Commons knowledge graph. This is a pilot operationalization of progression influence, not a validated measure of instructional importance.
metrics.inputDescription: futureDependentStandards.length for the misconception's ccssStandard in the knowledge-graph response. Pilot proxy: the query returns buildsTowards at the STANDARD level; learning-component edges are not fetched. null when the standard is not in the response.
metrics.weightNote: Weighted 1 against 3 for the other metrics, so progression informs the ranking without deciding it. The doc's 0-3 scale is unchanged; only its share of the total is reduced. Reason: in this pilot the count is taken at the standard level and only two of its four levels are reachable on the standards we fetch (1 and 3), so a one-level difference here was cancelling a two-level difference in share of class - a misconception affecting 11% of the class was outranking one affecting 43%.

metrics.label: Student Confidence
metrics.description: Average self-reported confidence of students exhibiting the misconception, based on the MIU confidence scale. Higher scores indicate greater confidence despite answering incorrectly.
metrics.inputDescription: Mean of the 1–5 confidence ratings on the linked wrong picks, counted alongside reach. null when no linked pick carried a rating.

bands.label: ≥ 4.0 — High confidence: students were highly confident despite answering incorrectly, suggesting a strongly held misconception.
≥ 3.0 & < 4.0 — Moderate-to-high confidence: students were generally confident despite answering incorrectly.
≥ 2.0 & < 3.0 — Low-to-moderate confidence: students showed some confidence despite answering incorrectly.
< 2.0 — Low confidence: students were generally uncertain about their incorrect responses.

metrics.label: Score on LC Misconception Evaluator
metrics.description: Score produced by the Learning Commons Misconception Evaluator for an identified misconception, providing complementary external evidence alongside MicroCoach's custom evaluation metrics. Normalize the LC score to a 0–3 scale using: 3 × (LC score / 100).
metrics.inputDescription: Raw 0–100 evaluator score. No integration exists yet; the slot is reserved.

metrics.label: Conceptual Depth
metrics.description: The extent to which a misconception reflects an underlying misunderstanding of the mathematical concept or mental model, rather than primarily an error in carrying out a mathematical procedure or algorithm. Higher Conceptual Depth indicates that the misconception reflects a more fundamental conceptual misunderstanding.

levels.0: The misconception primarily reflects an error in carrying out a mathematical procedure or algorithm. The underlying mathematical concept appears largely intact.
levels.1: The misconception reflects mostly procedural difficulty, but there is some evidence of incomplete or emerging conceptual understanding.
levels.2: The misconception reflects an incorrect or incomplete understanding of an important mathematical concept, although students may still demonstrate partial conceptual understanding.
levels.3: The misconception reflects a fundamentally incorrect mental model or core mathematical idea that is likely to affect reasoning across multiple problems or contexts.

selection.description: MicroCoach surfaces up to three identified misconceptions and highlights the highest-scoring misconception as the Recommended Focus for the teacher.
selection.rankOnDescription: total / maxPossible, so a misconception missing one metric (e.g. its standard was not in the graph) is not penalized against peers. Session-wide gaps (no confidence data, LC disabled) affect every misconception equally.
selection.tiebreakDescription: Not specified in the doc. Higher wins at each step; inputOrder is the order the misconceptions were given, so the result is deterministic.
selection.maxScoreNote: Each metric scores 0-3 per the doc; the total is the weighted sum, so the maximum is sum(3 x weight) over the ENABLED metrics: 30 as configured (frequency, progression, confidence, depth), or 39 if the LC evaluator is enabled at weight 3. Ranking is on total / maxPossible, so the weights change ordering, not the scale the scores are reported on.

llm.description: One call over all misconceptions returns conceptualDepth 0–3 plus a one-sentence justification each. The level definitions above are the whole scale the model is given.
